subject: Concierge integration: commission approval flow and capped revshare
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan@cloudsmith.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concierge integration pilot: revenue share and lead lock

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking the call last week — CloudSmith is excited to pilot the Concierge integration. Attached is the initial MOU and a suggested commission outline. A few items we need to lock ASAP so our sales team can start registering early-stage opportunities: 

- Confirmation of the revenue-share tiers for the pilot (we suggested 70/30 first 6 months, then step-down).
- Opportunity lock / lead registration protections (we typically ask for 180 days).
- Demo credit and co-selling rules for joint proofs-of-concept.
- Escrow/holdback language for chargebacks and refunds.

Attached: CloudSmith_MOU_v1.pdf

Can you confirm who on your side will handle the commission schedule and who we should route registration requests to? If possible, we'd love a short mutual action plan this week — signer + timeline + acceptance criteria.

cc: partner_success@cloudsmith.io

Appreciate it,
Jordan Park
Head of Partnerships | CloudSmith
jordan@cloudsmith.io

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan@cloudsmith.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concierge integration pilot: revenue share and lead lock

Jordan — thanks for the MOU. Welcome again — we're excited to get CloudSmith into the partner program. Quick read-through and high-level notes below. I'm copying Marissa (partner ops), Ben (rev ops) and Logan (legal) so we can align on sign-off.

High-level asks / proposed edits:
- Rev-share cap: OK to do a stepped rev-share for the pilot, but Redwood needs an overall cap per-customer per-year for the first 12 months to avoid outsized exposure. Suggest cap = $150k gross rev per-customer for pilot tiering.
- Introduction/lead lock: 180-day registration window is reasonable, but we need explicit proof-of-intro criteria (CRM note + registration form + demo attendance) to qualify.
- Demo credit: we'll provide a one-time $5k demo credit on customers that progress to paid within 90 days; credit counts against first invoice.
- Holdback/clawback: propose 6-month clawback window with monthly amortization for refunds/chargebacks; escrow language should reference invoice-level adjustments rather than gross revenue.
- Approval flow: Marissa to own partner onboarding checklist; Ben to own commission math and payout cadence; Logan to sign legal redlines.

Next steps I propose this week:
1) Ben to produce a clean commission waterfall (tier thresholds + payout timing).
2) Logan to review MOU redlines and produce a single redline PDF.
3) Marissa to create a mutual action plan doc and assign the DocuSign owner.

If that works, I'll push back a draft mutual action plan by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Strategic Alliances | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment: noted (CloudSmith_MOU_v1.pdf referenced)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan@cloudsmith.io>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concierge integration pilot: revenue share and lead lock

On Mon, Jun 9, 2025 at 11:03 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the MOU. Welcome again — we're excited to get CloudSmith into the partner program.

Folks — attached is a proposed commission_schedule.xlsx with a waterfall that matches Soojin's constraints while keeping the pilot commercially attractive. Key points:

- Proposed tiers (pilot): 70/30 for first $100k ARR sourced by CloudSmith, 60/40 for next $100k, then 50/50 beyond that within the 12-month pilot window.
- Annual cap: implemented as a per-customer gross revenue cap of $150k for 12 months.
- Payout timing: monthly reconciliation, pay-out on Net 45 after invoicing to avoid rhythm issues with refunds.
- Clawback mechanics: 6-month straight-line amortization on refunds, tracked at invoice level; adjustments captured in the next monthly reconciliation.

Open questions for legal (Logan):
- Is the proposed per-customer cap enforceable with standard MOU language or should it be in an SOW?
- For demo credits treated as invoice credits, any tax/compliance flags we should flag?

I dropped a Jira ticket for the finance side: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRJ-231 — please comment on the schedule tab in the attached spreadsheet.

Attachment: commission_schedule.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Jordan Park <jordan@cloudsmith.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, partner_success@cloudsmith.io
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concierge integration pilot: revenue share and lead lock

Soojin / team — thanks for the quick alignment and for Ben's detailed waterfall. CloudSmith is fine with the per-customer cap and the 6-month clawback amortization; the demo credit structure also sounds workable.

Next items from our side: 
- I'll get legal to redline the MOU to reflect the cap, registration proof criteria, and the clawback language — we'll send that by EOD Thursday.
- We prefer DocuSign for signatures; will send a signing link once we have your redline.
- For registration, we'll route forms to Marissa at partnerops@cloudsmith.io and mark the CRM lead with \"CloudSmith Intro\" + date. Please confirm that CRM notes + completed registration form are sufficient for lock.
